Thanks for the demo last week. Solara is moving the POC into our security review and we have a few specific asks to close the privacy gate:

2) Confirmation of Art. 28 (processor) subprocessor arrangements and the most recent subprocessor inventory; we understand you have third-party cloud infra and a couple of managed services. A sanitized export would be fine.
3) The security annex you attach to your DPA (we need the current exhibit language to align to our legal checklist).
4) A short attestation that Redwood will support our DPIA (30–45 minutes call) and provide operational evidence (logs / access controls) if required.

Target timeline: ideally we need the materials by end of week (Friday 03/26) to get legal sign-off before our April board review. Are you able to provide these items and a one-hour slot for a DPIA walkthrough?

Adding a couple of technical details for the packet and what I will include in the sanitized export:

- Subprocessor export: name, role (infra/monitoring/backup), country, data categories processed, last security assessment date. We will remove any account-specific hostnames or customer IDs. Format: CSV (sanitized).
- Article 30 excerpt: scope will list processing activities for tokenization, ephemeral KV cache usage, telemetry (anonymized), and retention for logs.
- KMS / key management: we will provide the KMS provider name and whether keys are customer-managed (for Dedicated/Private customers) or Redwood-managed for hosted.
- Logs: we can provide sample access log extracts and a description of retention and indexing (not full raw logs in the first pass).

Attachments I’ll push to the Drive packet: redwood_subprocessor_export_sanitized.csv (stub), redwood_article30_register_excerpt.pdf (stub), and a short readme describing redaction rules. If Solara needs a formal ISO/SOC snapshot, that will be a separate request — we can include our SOC 2 summary in the packet.
